blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Reliable validation of machine learning models is a crucial step in designing robust and trustworthy systems. Yet validation relies on annotated test sets treated as ground truth, even though annotations can be noisy or ambiguous. In object detection, sources may disagree on object presence, box location, or class label. Standard agreement metrics usually binarize box overlap before computing a summary score, obscuring the degree and structure of disagreement between annotation sets. Here, we study an Optimal Transport (OT)-based metric for measuring agreement between object detection annotations. Instead of binarizing bounding box overlap, this metric assigns graded costs to matched and unmatched labeled boxes. Through theoretical analysis and experiments on real and synthetically perturbed annotations, we show that OT captures graded changes in agreement and distinguishes annotation pairs that thresholded metrics score identically. Our results suggest that OT provides a richer measure of annotation agreement in object detection, especially for domains with many small or ambiguous objects. Such agreement estimates can support more reliable validation when labels are noisy or conflicting.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Modern machine learning systems rely on annotated data for training and
validation, typically treating a fixed test set as a gold standard .
Yet a single noise-free ground truth may not exist: multiple plausible
annotations can arise from task ambiguity, limited visual evidence, or
differences in expert judgment. This is especially relevant in object
detection, where annotators may disagree on object presence, spatial
extent, or class labels [ 4 , 14 , 21 ] .
Such disagreement contains information about the reliability of the
reference data. A prediction that differs from one annotation may remain
consistent with another plausible interpretation, so performance against
a single reference can obscure annotation uncertainty. Measuring
agreement is therefore important for assessing both dataset quality and
the reliability of model validation.

blocks.en: Agreement in object detection is commonly assessed by matching boxes with an Intersection-over-Union (IoU) threshold and then computing a summary statistic such as F1 or Krippendorff’s α \alpha [ 9 , 22 ] . This approach is simple and useful, but the thresholding step discards spatial information. After overlap is converted into a binary match decision, the resulting score may no longer reflect how close the boxes are, how severe the mismatch is, or how unmatched boxes are arranged. Thus, annotation pairs with different spatial structure can receive the same agreement score.
blocks.zh: 通常通过将相交-交叉-联盟(IoU)阈值相匹配的框来评估物体探测方面的一致,然后计算F1或Krippendorff的α-α[9,22]等汇总统计. 这种方法简单而有用,但门槛步骤会丢弃空间信息. 重叠被转换为二进制匹配决定后,产生的分数可能再不能反映相框的相近程度,不匹配的严重程度,或者未匹配相框的排列方式. 因此,具有不同空间结构的注释对可以得到同样的协议分数.

blocks.en: In this work, we study an Optimal Transport (OT)-based metric for measuring agreement between object detection annotations. The formulation builds on recent OT-based work for object detection evaluation [ 15 ] , but shifts the focus from comparing model predictions with a reference to comparing annotation sets themselves. Each annotation is treated as a set of labeled bounding boxes, and agreement is computed through a transport problem whose cost combines localization, label consistency, and penalties for unmatched boxes.

blocks.en: 2.1 Uncertainty and disagreement in object detection annotations
blocks.zh: 2.1 物体探测说明中的不确定性和分歧

blocks.en:
Annotation uncertainty has been addressed by modeling label noise or
learning from repeated annotations [ 21 , 25 ] ,
using richer targets such as label distributions [ 7 , 27 , 18 ] ,
representing localization uncertainty probabilistically [ 11 ] ,
and aggregating annotations into a latent ground truth [ 25 , 10 , 26 ] .
Other work characterizes model performance under contradictory
labels [ 23 ] . Our goal is complementary: we measure
pairwise agreement and discrepancy directly between object detection
annotations, either to characterize annotation quality or as a component
of multi-reference validation.

blocks.en: 2.3 Optimal transport for detection evaluation
blocks.zh: 2.3 检测评价的最佳运输方式

blocks.en: Optimal Transport provides a natural framework for comparing structured sets by computing a minimum-cost assignment between elements. With dummy elements or related unbalanced formulations, it can also account for unmatched or poorly matched elements. More broadly, transport-style objectives have been used to compare distributions, align structured representations, and solve set-matching problems [ 6 , 3 , 20 ] .
blocks.zh: 优化运输提供了一个自然框架,通过计算要素之间的最低成本分配来比较结构组。 有了假元素或相關的不平衡配方,它也可以说明未配对或配比差的元素. 更广泛地说,运输式目标被用来比较分布,调整结构化的表示,并解决组合匹配问题[6,3,20].

blocks.en: In object detection, Otani et al. [ 15 ] proposed an OT-based evaluation metric, Optimal Correction Cost (OC-cost), building on earlier work [ 16 , 6 ] . OC-cost compares detector predictions with ground-truth boxes and penalizes localization errors, label mismatches, false positives, and false negatives within a single transport problem. This produces a fine-grained measure of detection quality and addresses limitations of standard mAP-style evaluation.
blocks.zh: 在物体探测中,Otani等. [15] 提出了基于OT的评价衡量标准,优化校正成本(OC-cost),以先前的工作为基础[16,6]. OC成本将探测器预测与地上真能箱进行比较,并在一个单一的运输问题中惩罚本地化出错,标签不匹配,假阳性,假阴性. 这产生了对检测质量的精细衡量,并解决了标准mAP式评价的局限性.

blocks.en: Our work uses the same general OT perspective but changes the object of comparison. Rather than evaluating detector predictions against a fixed ground truth with confidence scores, we compare annotation sets directly. This shift removes the need to treat either annotation as error-free and allows OT to serve as a measure of annotation agreement or discrepancy. In this setting, the transport cost captures spatial proximity, label consistency, and missing or extra boxes, providing a graded alternative to thresholded agreement metrics.
blocks.zh: 我们的作品采用了相同的总体OT视角,但改变了比较的对象. 我们不是用信心分数来评估探测器的预测,而是直接比较注释集。 这种转变消除了将注解视为无出错的必要性,并允许OT作为注解协议或差异的衡量标准. 在这个设置中,运输成本能捕捉空间相近性,标签一致性,以及缺失或额外框,提供分级的替代阈值协议度量表.

blocks.en: We next study how the OT score behaves under simplified settings that make the transport plan interpretable. For arbitrary annotations, the optimal plan depends on the number of boxes, labels, and hyperparameters and must generally be computed numerically. To obtain analytical insight, we consider special cases in which the matching structure is known or can be approximated. These cases clarify how the score depends on object count, spatial mismatch, and the dummy-matching penalty.

Fig. 2(a) shows the theoretical CDF of the box-matching cost as a function of β \beta under Uniform and Half-Normal perturbations, together with empirical estimates on ACNE04 [ 27 ] . For visualization, we use the annotation set from [ 8 ] , which contains substantially more objects than the original annotation. Each curve corresponds to a different noise level γ \gamma .
As β \beta increases, a perturbed box is more likely to match a real box rather than the dummy box, because β \beta sets the penalty for unmatched boxes. Higher noise levels shift the curves toward larger β \beta : when boxes are strongly perturbed, real-real matches require a larger dummy penalty to remain preferable.
The theoretical and empirical curves agree well for small perturbations, where each perturbed box remains close to its original counterpart. The discrepancy grows at higher noise levels. In this regime, a perturbed box may become closer to a different object than to the box from which it was generated, violating the noisy-box assumption used in the derivation. This deviation is informative: it indicates that the two annotations are no longer related by simple localization noise, but differ more substantially in spatial structure.

blocks.en:
Fig. 3 shows example OT scores comparing two annotations for the ACNE04 dataset (Fig. 3(a) ) and for the TexBiG dataset (Fig. 3(b) ), along with the theoretical boundaries in Eq. 10 . There are two key differences between these sets of annotations. First, acne objects generally have a smaller size relative to the image resolution than objects on paper (such as paragraphs or headings), meaning that changes in localization affect the cost metric much more strongly in the former case. Second, when an object is easy to annotate (e.g. a clearly visible paragraph in a document), it can naturally be surrounded by a rectangular box. From the figures one can clearly see that, while for ACNE04 we obtain a wide range of OT values, for TexBiG almost all objects lie close to the upper bound: localization error rarely becomes crucial.
Based on these observations, we believe that the OT score can be applied to any dataset, but it is most useful and informative when there are many small or medium-sized boxes in specialized domains (e.g. acne-lesion detection), where objects can be easily missed or misclassified.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we adapted an Optimal Transport (OT)–based metric for quantifying annotator agreement in object detection. By formulating agreement as a transport problem between sets of bounding boxes, our approach naturally integrates spatial and label information and allows for flexible handling of missing or extra annotations.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们调整了一个基于最佳运输(OT)的衡量标准,用于量化物体探测中的注释者协议。 通过将协议作为各套捆绑箱之间的运输问题,我们的方法自然将空间和标签信息结合起来,并允许灵活处理缺失或附加说明。

blocks.en: We analyzed several theoretical properties of the OT-based metric, deriving bounds for cases in which the transport plan is known and characterizing the possible range of OT scores under specific parameter settings. We also studied the behavior of the metric as a function of β \beta under a noisy-box assumption. This analysis helps to understand how many real matches remain as β \beta or the noise level increases, how to select β \beta for a given task, and when deviations from the theoretical assumptions signal that annotations have become substantially different.
blocks.zh: 我们分析了以OT为基础的度量衡的几个理论属性,为已知运输计划的情况设定了界限,并说明了在特定参数设置下OT分数的可能范围。 我们还研究了在高音箱假设下作为β\β函数的度量衡的行为. 这种分析有助于了解在β\β或噪声水平增加时到底有多少个真匹配还存在,如何为特定任务选择β\β,当偏离理论假设的信号说明说明变得大相径庭时.

blocks.en: Through experiments on both real-world and synthetically perturbed datasets, we demonstrated that the OT-based metric is particularly sensitive to differences in annotations, especially with respect to the spatial positions of bounding boxes. In scenarios where traditional IoU threshold-based metrics (such as F1 or Krippendorff’s α \alpha ) fail to distinguish between qualitatively different annotation patterns, OT still reflects meaningful variation in annotator behavior.
blocks.zh: 通过对现实世界和合成扰动数据集的实验,我们表明,基于OT的衡量标准对说明的不同特别敏感,特别是在边框的空间位置方面。 在传统的IoU阈值测量法(如F1或Krippendorff的α-α-α)无法区分质地不同的注解模式的情况下,OT仍然反映了注解者行为的有意义的变化.

blocks.en: Our findings lead to two main conclusions. First, model performance evaluation and annotator agreement assessment are closely related but not identical: what is treated as an “error” in model evaluation does not necessarily correspond to disagreement between annotators, and OT can help to disentangle these notions. Second, because the main sensitivity of the OT cost comes from spatial localization, we believe it is especially well suited to domains with many small or medium-sized boxes and non-trivial domain knowledge (e.g. medical imaging), where objects are easily missed or misclassified.
blocks.zh: 我们的调查结果得出了两个主要结论。 首先,模型性能评价和注释员协议评估密切相关,但并不相同:模型评价中被视为“错误”的东西不一定对应注释员之间的分歧,而OT可以帮助分解这些概念。 第二,由于OT成本的主要灵敏度来自空间局部化,我们认为它特别适合拥有许多中小盒子和非三角域知识(如医学成像)的域,在这些域中,物体很容易被忽略或被误分类.

blocks.en: Overall, these results indicate that the OT metric provides a richer and more informative measure of annotator agreement and discrepancy, and can support more reliable model validation in the presence of noisy or conflicting labels.
blocks.zh: 总的来说,这些结果表明,OT度量法提供了更丰富和内容更丰富的注释协议和差异度量,并且可以在有吵闹或相冲突标签的情况下支持更可靠的模型验证.

In Fig. 2(a) , the annotations differ by a moderate spatial shift: the objects are localized approximately correctly, although the boxes are not perfectly aligned. In Fig. 2(b) , one annotation has been deliberately shifted so that only one pair of boxes overlaps, while the remaining boxes are far from their corresponding objects.

blocks.en: F1 and Krippendorff’s α \alpha assign the same values to both cases, because after thresholded matching there is one true positive and the remaining boxes are treated as unmatched errors. This is appropriate for counting detection errors, but it loses information that matters for annotation agreement. The first pair reflects approximate agreement with localization noise, whereas the second reflects a stronger spatial disagreement. The OT score distinguishes these cases because unmatched and poorly matched boxes still contribute through their spatial costs. Mean IoU also reflects part of this difference, but only while corresponding boxes overlap; once overlap is zero, it cannot distinguish larger spatial displacements. Thus, OT provides a graded comparison of bounding-box annotations beyond the binary matched/unmatched decisions used by thresholded metrics.

blocks.en: Fig. 5 shows the empirical CDF of bounding-box area relative to image size, highlighting differences in object size across the datasets used in this paper. For Acne04 and AcneSCU, objects are relatively small: the vast majority of boxes occupy less than 1% of the image area. Although many small boxes are also present, the median relative area is approximately 7%, and there is a substantial number of objects that cover 30% or more of the image. These differences in object size across datasets help illustrate how the proposed approach behaves in distinct, realistic scenarios.
